items.title: 1.4 Three Cube Roots of Unity (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Is sabaq mein hum number 1 ke teen cube roots dhoondenge. Shayad aap sochein: "1 ka cube root to sirf 1 hai, kyun ke \(1 \times 1 \times 1 = 1\)." Real numbers ki had tak aap bilkul sahi hain. Lekin complex numbers ki duniya mein do aur numbers bhi aise hain jin ka cube 1 hai. Pichle sabaq mein aap ne seekha tha ke degree \(n\) wali equation ke bilkul \(n\) roots hote hain; \(x^{3} = 1\) degree 3 ki equation hai, to us ke teen roots hone chahiye. Aaiye unhein dhoondte hain.
Pehle lafz samajh lein: "unity" ka matlab hai number 1. Cube root of unity woh number hai jis ka cube (teesri power) 1 ho. Maan lijiye \(x\) unity ka ek cube root hai. To:

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yahan har line mein kya hua, dekhiye. Power \(\frac{1}{3}\) ka matlab cube root hai; dono sides ka cube lene se \(x^{3} = 1\) aaya. Phir 1 ko left side le aaye taa ke equation "= 0" wali shakal mein ho, kyun ke factorization ke baad hi hum roots nikaal sakte hain.
Factorization is formula se hui hai: \(a^{3} - b^{3} = (a - b)(a^{2} + ab + b^{2})\), jahan \(a = x\) aur \(b = 1\). Aap multiply kar ke khud check kar sakte hain: \((x - 1)(x^{2} + x + 1) = x^{3} + x^{2} + x - x^{2} - x - 1 = x^{3} - 1\).
Ab ek bunyadi usool: do cheezon ka product zero tabhi hota hai jab un mein se koi ek zero ho. Is liye humein do alag equations mil jati hain.

Ya to \(x - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 1\) (yeh woh root hai jo hum pehle se jaante the), ya \(x^{2} + x + 1 = 0\). Yeh quadratic factor nahin hota, is liye quadratic formula lagate hain, jahan \(a = b = c = 1\):

\[x = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1-4}}{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{-3}}{2}\]
Formula \(x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^{2} - 4ac}}{2a}\) mein \(b = 1\) rakha, is liye shuru mein \(-b = -1\) aata hai; aur andar \(b^{2} - 4ac = 1 - 4 = -3\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab beech wale step mein \(\frac{1 \pm \sqrt{3}i}{2}\) likhti hai, yani \(-1\) ka minus sign reh gaya hai. Sahi yeh hai: \(x = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1-4}}{2} = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{-3}}{2} = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\), jaise kitab ki agli line mein theek likha hai. Aap apni copy mein minus zaroor likhiye.

\[\Rightarrow x = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\]
\[(\because \sqrt{-1} = i)\]
Yahan \(\sqrt{-3} = \sqrt{3}\sqrt{-1} = \sqrt{3}\,i\) likha gaya hai; yahi woh jagah hai jahan \(i\) humari madad ko aata hai.
Is tarah unity ke teen cube roots yeh hain:

blocks.text_alt: 1, minus 1 plus root 3 i over 2, and minus 1 minus root 3 i over 2

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Hum jaante hain ke jin numbers mein \(i\) ho, unhein Complex numbers kehte hain. Is liye \(\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\) aur \(\frac{-1-\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\) ko unity ke complex ya imaginary cube roots kaha jata hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kitab mein \(\sqrt{3}i\) ka matlab \(\sqrt{3}\cdot i\) hai, yani \(i\) square root ke bahar hai, andar nahin.
Kya waqai \(\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\) ka cube 1 hai? Chaliye check karte hain. Is ka square: \(\frac{1 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i - 3}{4} = \frac{-1-\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\), yani doosra complex root! Ab dono complex roots ko multiply karein: \(\frac{(-1)^{2} - (\sqrt{3}\,i)^{2}}{4} = \frac{1 + 3}{4} = 1\). Matlab root \(\times\) root\(^{2}\) = root\(^{3}\) = 1. Is ka cube sach mein 1 hai.
Ek aur baat ghor karne wali hai: dono complex roots ek doosre ke conjugate (sirf imaginary part ka sign ulta, jaise aaine mein aks) hain.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Unity ke cube roots woh numbers hain jo \(x^{3} = 1\) ko poora karte hain: \(1\), \(\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\), \(\frac{-1-\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\).
2. Yeh \((x - 1)(x^{2} + x + 1) = 0\) se aate hain; pehla factor 1 deta hai, doosra quadratic formula se do complex roots.
3. Ek root real (1) hai aur baaqi do complex conjugates hain.
4. Degree 3 ki equation, is liye teen roots: Fundamental theorem of algebra ki ek aur misaal.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Yeh kehna ke 1 ka sirf ek cube root hai: \(C\) mein teen hain.
2. Quadratic formula mein \(-b\) ka minus kho dena (kitab khud ek line mein yeh karti hai): \(b = 1\) ho to \(-b = -1\). Bachne ka tareeqa: formula likhne se pehle \(a, b, c\) aur \(-b\) alag likh lein.
3. \(\sqrt{-3} = -\sqrt{3}\) likh dena: sahi \(\sqrt{3}\,i\) hai.
4. \(\sqrt{3}i\) ko \(\sqrt{3i}\) samajh lena: \(i\) root ke bahar hai.
